# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

You review one branch of gba-emu, an original GBA emulator in Rust, before it is merged into `main`.
You did not write this code, and you have not seen the author's reasoning. Judge the diff on its own.

Read `CLAUDE.md` and `PLAN.md` first. Then run `git diff main...<branch>` for the branch named in your task.

1. **Correctness vs spec.** For each hardware behaviour the diff implements, find the gbatek section

   (shift by 0/32, misaligned access, register r15 as operand, mode banking), bit positions, and cycle counts.
2. **Ownership.** The diff touches only the files the worker's role owns (PLAN.md tables). List any other file.

   to make one test pass.
4. **Originality.** Flag anything that looks taken from another emulator rather than written from gbatek:
   naming or structure from a known emulator (mGBA, NanoBoyAdvance, VBA, Mesen, gba-core), comments
   referring to other emulators, magic tables or behaviour that gbatek does not explain, or large blocks
   unlike the rest of the codebase. Do not open other emulators' source to compare. Use the spec and
   your judgement, and explain each flag.

  GBA Timers

The GBA includes four incrementing 16bit timers.
Timer 0 and 1 can be used to supply the sample rate for DMA sound channel A
and/or B.

4000100h - TM0CNT_L - Timer 0 Counter/Reload (R/W)
4000104h - TM1CNT_L - Timer 1 Counter/Reload (R/W)
4000108h - TM2CNT_L - Timer 2 Counter/Reload (R/W)
400010Ch - TM3CNT_L - Timer 3 Counter/Reload (R/W)
Writing to these registers initializes the <reload> value (but does not
directly affect the current counter value). Reading returns the current
<counter> value (or the recent/frozen counter value if the timer has been
stopped).
The reload value is copied into the counter only upon following two situations:
Automatically upon timer overflows, or when the timer start bit becomes changed
from 0 to 1.
Note: When simultaneously changing the start bit from 0 to 1, and setting the
reload value at the same time (by a single 32bit I/O operation), then the newly
written reload value is recognized as new counter value.

4000102h - TM0CNT_H - Timer 0 Control (R/W)
4000106h - TM1CNT_H - Timer 1 Control (R/W)
400010Ah - TM2CNT_H - Timer 2 Control (R/W)
400010Eh - TM3CNT_H - Timer 3 Control (R/W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-1   Prescaler Selection (0=F/1, 1=F/64, 2=F/256, 3=F/1024)
  2     Count-up Timing   (0=Normal, 1=See below)  ;Not used in TM0CNT_H
  3-5   Not used
  6     Timer IRQ Enable  (0=Disable, 1=IRQ on Timer overflow)
  7     Timer Start/Stop  (0=Stop, 1=Operate)
  8-15  Not used

When Count-up Timing is enabled, the prescaler value is ignored, instead the
time is incremented each time when the previous counter overflows. This
function cannot be used for Timer 0 (as it is the first timer).
F = System Clock (16.78MHz).





  
  GBA DMA Transfers

Overview
The GBA includes four DMA channels, the highest priority is assigned to DMA0,
followed by DMA1, DMA2, and DMA3. DMA Channels with lower priority are paused
until channels with higher priority have completed.
The CPU is paused when DMA transfers are active, however, the CPU is operating
during the periods when Sound/Blanking DMA transfers are paused.

Special features of the separate DMA channels
DMA0 - highest priority, best for timing critical transfers (eg. HBlank DMA).
DMA1 and DMA2 - can be used to feed digital sample data to the Sound FIFOs.
DMA3 - can be used to write to Game Pak ROM/FlashROM (but not GamePak SRAM).
Aside from that, each DMA 0-3 may be used for whatever general purposes.

40000B0h,0B2h - DMA0SAD - DMA 0 Source Address (W) (internal memory)
40000BCh,0BEh - DMA1SAD - DMA 1 Source Address (W) (any memory)
40000C8h,0CAh - DMA2SAD - DMA 2 Source Address (W) (any memory)
40000D4h,0D6h - DMA3SAD - D

I found no blockers and no correctness bugs against gbatek. The changes are within the allowed files, there are no per-ROM hacks, and both graded timer tests now pass. The findings are one latent integration issue and some small gaps.

**Checks run** (branch worktree `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a43403a18caac5e09`, at c105937):
- **Tests and build:** `cargo test` passes (83 tests) and the wasm release build succeeds.
- **Grading, branch vs main:**

| Test | Branch | Main |
|---|---|---|
| timer-reload | 1.0 | about 0 |
| timer-start-stop | 1.0 | about 0 |
| aw-arm-alu | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| aw-thumb-alu | 1.0 | 1.0 |

| dma-priority | 3.9e-08 | 3.9e-08 |
| tonc-snd1 | 0.984 | 0.984 |

  No smoke-set test scores lower than on main.
- **Ownership:** the diff touches only `src/timer.rs`, plus the two `catch_up` calls in `src/io.rs` and the overflow-count loop in `src/gba.rs`, which you authorised. The return type of `Timers::step` changed from a `u8` bit mask to `[u32; 4]` overflow counts. That is a contract change, but it is the change you approved.
- **Spec:** checked against gbatek "GBA Timers". The reload value is copied into the counter only on overflow or on a stop-to-start change. A 32-bit write sets the new reload and starts the timer in one go: `io_write32` writes the low half first, and both halves fall in the same delayed cycle. Unused control bits are cleared, the prescaler shifts are 0/6/8/10, cascading works, and the count-up bit is ignored on timer 0. Repeated overflows within one step are handled correctly, and the arithmetic in `count()` cannot overflow.

**Findings**
- /var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a43403a18caac5e09/src/timer.rs:131: [major] Two counters can get out of step once the DMA branch merges. `catch_up` takes `bus.access_cycles` as "cycles since the last step", but the CPU clears `access_cycles` in `take_access_cycles()` before `dma::run_pending_transfers` runs. Meanwhile the timers' `cycles_already_run` still counts the CPU part of the step. A DMA that reads or writes timer registers would then measure time from the wrong starting point, so the timers stand still and `step` skips the wrong cycles. It works today only because DMA is a stub. Suggested fix: give the timers one cycle base that DMA also uses (for example, the bus keeps a running count of cycles since the last component step), or have the integrator raise this when DMA merges.
- /var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a43403a18caac5e09/src/timer.rs:86: [minor] Timer 0 with the count-up bit set gets `start_delay = 0`, yet `advance` (correctly) clocks it from the prescaler. Its start is therefore one cycle earlier than a normal timer's. Suggested fix: decide "is count-up" with the same rule as `advance`, i.e. index > 0 and the bit set; this needs the timer index passed in, or a check in `Timers`.
- /var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a43403a18caac5e09/src/timer.rs:20: [minor] `WRITE_DELAY_CYCLES` and `START_DELAY_CYCLES` were tuned against the grader because gbatek does not give these delays. The project rules allow this and the comment says so. It is not a per-ROM hack, but it is fragile, as the comment admits. No change needed; flagged for awareness.
- /var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a43403a18caac5e09/src/gba.rs:81: [minor] FIFO ticks are delivered one per overflow in a loop. With prescaler F/1 and reload 0xFFFF, a full halted frame means about 280k calls to `apu.on_timer_overflow`. That is acceptable for now. Suggested fix: add a `ponytail:` comment, or have the APU take a count once FIFO ticks are implemented.
- /var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a43403a18caac5e09/src/timer.rs:226: [minor] Some behaviour has no unit test: the gbatek note on a single 32-bit write that sets the reload and starts the timer, count-up being ignored on timer 0, and overflow IRQs raised from inside `catch_up` or a write delay. Suggested fix: add one small test for each.

**Readability and originality:** names are clear, register constants have plain-English comments, and the non-obvious functions have doc comments naming the gbatek section. The design (bulk ticks per step, a start delay, catch-up before each register access) follows from gbatek plus the measured delays. I saw no naming, structure or tables from another emulator.
